electric.name: Duke Energy Carolinas
electric.serves: About 2.3 million households and businesses in central and western North Carolina, 'including Charlotte, Durham and the Triad' (July 17, 2026). It has 3 million customers across a 24,000-square-mile area in NC and SC.

gas.name: Piedmont Natural Gas
gas.serves: Duke Energy subsidiary distributing gas to more than 1.2 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina and Tennessee (Jan. 16, 2026). Charlotte and the surrounding area are among 'the communities it serves' (July 13, 2026).

utilities.notes: Both duke-energy.com and piedmontng.com returned HTTP 403 to automated requests, so their program pages could not be read. Duke and Piedmont details here come from Duke's official newsroom (news.duke-energy.com) and are dated. City-owned systems and electric co-ops in outlying counties, and utilities on the South Carolina side (Chester, Lancaster, York), were not researched.

auditPrograms.name: Duke Energy Home Energy House Call
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Duke Energy Carolinas residential customers. Detailed eligibility rules (home type, ownership, usage history) were not verified because duke-energy.com blocked automated access.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: A home energy assessment, a customized usage report, low-cost tips, expert recommendations and a free energy-efficiency kit. Since Jan. 1, 2025 it also includes free products customized to the home and installed at no charge, with virtual assessments for eligible customers.
auditPrograms.howToBook: Sign up through the Home Energy House Call page on duke-energy.com, linked from Duke's 2026 news releases. The booking page was not read.

auditPrograms.name: Energy Saver North Carolina (HOMES) home energy assessment
auditPrograms.runBy: NC Department of Environmental Quality, State Energy Office
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: NC homeowners and renters (with landlord approval) with household income under 150% of area median income, after income eligibility is confirmed.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: A certified assessor does a free home energy assessment. You then review quotes from Energy Saver NC-registered contractors with the rebate already applied.
auditPrograms.howToBook: Start the prequalification form at energysavernc.org, or call 866-998-8555 (Mon-Fri 8-5).
auditPrograms.status: open (available in all 100 NC counties since 2026-02-10; first come, first served)

auditPrograms.name: Piedmont Natural Gas Energy Advisor
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Piedmont customers with an online account.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: An online tool showing 'how energy efficient their home is' and where to improve, based on the home's own data. Piedmont also offers water heater, cooking and dryer cost calculators.
auditPrograms.howToBook: Online through the customer's Piedmont account.
auditPrograms.status: open (online tool, per Piedmont release of 2026-01-16)

rebates.name: Energy Saver NC: HOMES (Homeowners Managing Efficiency Savings)
rebates.runBy: NC DEQ State Energy Office (federal IRA funds)
rebates.amount: Up to $16,000 for whole-home efficiency upgrades such as air sealing or efficient HVAC
rebates.whoQualifies: Homeowners and renters under 150% AMI. Under 80% AMI: up to 100% of project costs, up to a set amount. 80-150% AMI: up to 50%, up to a set amount. All work must be done by a registered contractor, and self-installs don't qualify. Enrollment in programs like LIEAP or Medicaid can qualify you for higher rebates without extra income checks.
rebates.status: open (statewide since 2026-02-10, including Mecklenburg; first come, first served; expected to run until 2031 or until funds run out)

rebates.name: Energy Saver NC: HEAR (Home Electrification and Appliance Rebates)
rebates.amount: Up to $14,000 per household. Caps: heat pump for space heating/cooling $8,000; electric panel $4,000; electric wiring $2,500 (the program page's rebate table says $2,000); heat pump water heater $1,750; insulation, air sealing and ventilation $1,600; heat pump dryer and/or electric stove/cooktop/range/oven $840.
rebates.whoQualifies: Households under 150% AMI (full coverage under 80%, up to 50% at 80-150%). Since Sept. 1, 2026, new and unreserved applications must follow DOE's new rules: 'Fuel Switching Projects are NOT allowed', so a gas or other fossil-fuel appliance can't be replaced with HEAR money. Replacing existing electric equipment with more efficient electric equipment is allowed, and insulation and air sealing may be required with heat pump projects.

rebates.name: Duke Energy Carolinas Smart $aver home improvement rebates (NC)
rebates.amount: From Jan. 1, 2025: 'HVAC, insulation, water heaters and heat pump incentives have increased from $350 to $500', and pool pump incentives went from $300 to $900.
rebates.whoQualifies: Duke Energy NC residential customers making qualifying energy-efficient upgrades (detailed requirements not verified).
rebates.status: unverified for 2026: amounts last confirmed in Duke's 2025-01-06 announcement; duke-energy.com program pages blocked automated access

rebates.name: Duke Energy Power Manager (smart thermostat / demand response)
rebates.amount: Smart thermostat programs: 'up to $150 in initial bill credits and $50 annually for qualifying devices' (March 6, 2026). Electric water heater owners get an extra $25 a year (new for 2025).
rebates.whoQualifies: Duke Energy Carolinas customers who enroll a qualifying smart thermostat or device in Power Manager.

rebates.name: Duke Energy Income-Qualified Weatherization (NC)
rebates.amount: Free measures. As of Jan. 1, 2025: HVAC replacement incentive up to $8,000 (up from $6,000) and refrigerator replacement $1,500 (up from $1,000).
rebates.whoQualifies: Duke Energy customers with income under 200% of federal poverty guidelines.
rebates.status: unverified for 2026: last confirmed in Duke's 2025-01-06 announcement

rebates.name: Duke Energy Neighborhood Energy $aver (NC)
rebates.amount: Free walk-through energy assessment and free energy-saving products
rebates.whoQualifies: Customers in qualifying neighborhoods, where 50% or more of residents have income under 200% of federal poverty guidelines.
rebates.status: unverified for 2026: last confirmed in Duke's 2025-01-06 announcement

rebates.name: Piedmont Natural Gas appliance rebates (NC)
rebates.status: unverified: piedmontng.com blocked automated access, and Piedmont's 2025-2026 winter releases mention tools and payment programs but no rebates

stateHomeEnergyRebates.status: open: available in all 100 NC counties since 2026-02-10 (HEAR rules changed 2026-09-01). The SC side of the metro is not launched.
stateHomeEnergyRebates.programName: Energy Saver North Carolina: HOMES and HEAR
stateHomeEnergyRebates.administrator: North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ), State Energy Office
stateHomeEnergyRebates.summary: Energy Saver NC launched Jan. 16, 2025 in a few counties and reached all 100 counties on Feb. 10, 2026. Wake and Mecklenburg were added last. Over $200 million is available. HOMES gives up to $16,000 and HEAR up to $14,000. Households under 80% AMI get up to 100% of costs (to set limits), 80-150% AMI up to 50%, and households over 150% AMI are not eligible. The process is: prequalify at energysavernc.org, get a free assessment, get quotes from registered contractors, receive approval, then the contractor is paid the rebate. Funding is first come, first served. After DOE's May 29, 2026 guidance, HEAR stopped funding fuel-switching on Sept. 1, 2026. South Carolina counties in the MSA (Chester, Lancaster, York): the SC Energy Office says 'Rebates are not currently available' and expects to launch HOMES (about $2,000-$16,000) and HEAR (up to $14,000, under 150% AMI) statewide in 2026.

incomeQualified.name: NC Weatherization Assistance Program: Charlotte-area providers
incomeQualified.runBy: NC DEQ State Energy Office through local agencies
incomeQualified.summary: Free weatherization for households under 200% of federal poverty guidelines (2026: 1 person $31,920; 2 $43,280; 3 $54,640; 4 $66,000) or receiving Work First or SSI. Annual WAP providers by county (NC agency finder): Blue Ridge Community Action (Mecklenburg, Gaston, Cabarrus, Union; 828-438-6255); ICARE (Iredell, Lincoln; 704-872-8141); Yadkin Valley Economic Development District (Rowan; 336-367-3535); Action Pathways (Anson; 910-485-6131). The separate IIJA-funded WAP is run by the Piedmont Triad Regional Council for Mecklenburg, Gaston, Iredell, Lincoln and Rowan (336-904-0338).

incomeQualified.name: Energy Saver NC for households under 80% AMI
incomeQualified.summary: Up to 100% of project costs (HOMES up to $16,000; HEAR up to $14,000), with no income verification needed if enrolled in programs like LIEAP or Medicaid.

incomeQualified.name: Duke Energy Income-Qualified Weatherization
incomeQualified.summary: Free conservation measures, including HVAC replacement up to $8,000, for Duke customers under 200% of federal poverty guidelines. Figures are from Duke's Jan. 6, 2025 announcement.

incomeQualified.name: Duke Energy Neighborhood Energy $aver
incomeQualified.summary: Free walk-through assessments and products in neighborhoods where 50%+ of residents are under 200% of federal poverty guidelines (Jan. 6, 2025 announcement).

localRules.name: No mandatory building energy benchmarking or performance standard (Charlotte / North Carolina)
localRules.appliesTo: Not applicable. Nothing affects homeowners or large buildings.

notes: MSA: CBSA 16740 (OMB July 2023): Anson, Cabarrus, Gaston, Iredell, Lincoln, Mecklenburg, Rowan and Union (NC); Chester, Lancaster and York (SC). The Energy Saver NC program page lists electric wiring at $2,500 in its FAQ but $2,000 in its rebate table. The Feb. 10, 2026 press release says $2,500. Duke Energy's program amounts for NC are from its Jan. 6, 2025 announcement (changes launched Jan. 1, 2025). Its 2026 releases confirm that Home Energy House Call and the smart thermostat credits are still offered but don't restate Smart $aver amounts. On the SC side, Duke raised residential incentives on Aug. 1, 2025 (Home Energy House Call with installed products, and Smart $aver rebates for insulation, water heaters and smart thermostats); amounts were not stated. SC-side WAP providers and SC utility programs (York, Lancaster, Chester counties) were not researched. The research tool's web-search budget ran out partway through, so Piedmont rebates and Duke 2026 program pages could not be confirmed another way. Federal tax credits: the IRS says the Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit (25C) can be claimed for improvements made through December 31, 2025, and the Residential Clean Energy Credit (25D) 'is not available for any property placed in service after December 31, 2025.' Do not list either as a current incentive. Federal rule change for the IRA rebates: DOE Program Notices 26-1 (HOMES) and 26-2 (HEAR/HEEHR), effective May 29, 2026, removed fuel-switching (gas/propane-to-electric) from HEAR so it now covers only electric-to-electric upgrades, and generally require insulation/air sealing to be addressed before heating and cooling upgrades. Launched states had to comply within three months; per NASEO's August 2026 FAQ, reservations made on or after September 1, 2026 must follow the new notices and DOE is extending award periods to September 30, 2031.
